subject: Northbridge discovery: SDK auth, routing & request/response schema questions
messages:
From: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@northbridge.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sejal Patel <sejal.patel@northbridge.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up + list of integration questions from today's demo

Thanks for the demo today — good session. Quick recap and a short list of technical/ops questions we need answered to scope the POC and internal kickoff. High level: we want an embeddings + reranker pipeline for search relevancy and a chat endpoint for agent-style product Q&A. Points below: 

1) SDK/auth: We prefer a server-side SDK approach. What auth modes do you support for private deployments (API key, OAuth client credentials, mTLS)? Any recommended best practice for short-lived credentials?

2) Routing/regions: We need requests to stay in us-east for data residency and fall back to us-west only on overload. How do we express routing policies? Can routing be per-route or per-API-key?

3) Request/response schema: For chat vs completions, do you recommend structured output (tool-calling / function outputs) for agent responses? How do you recommend handling token limits, stop sequences, and streaming semantics when using tool-calling?

4) Embeddings & rerankers: We plan to embed docs in-house and run a lightweight reranker. Any guidance on embedding dimensionality, vector store batch size, and whether to compute reranker signals via the generation endpoint or a separate rerank API?

5) Attachments & artifacts: Can you share a short sample request/response (chat with tool call + streaming) we can show our infra team?

If you can answer inline or point to a short doc/snippet that would be great. Happy to schedule a 30-min follow-up later this week to lock the POC scope.

Thanks,
Oliver
CTO, Northbridge Analytics

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@northbridge.ai>
Cc: Sejal Patel <sejal.patel@northbridge.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T17:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up + list of integration questions from today's demo

Oliver — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline, and then proposed next steps at the bottom. I'm copying our infra leads for deeper follow-up.

1) SDK/auth: Supported modes: API key (server-side), OAuth2 client_credentials (Private with our control plane), and mutual TLS for Private/on-prem deployments. Short-lived creds: we recommend issuing short-lived tokens via our token-exchange endpoint (we can mint tokens scoped to a route or model). We'll share a snippet in the Drive doc.

2) Routing/regions: Routing policies are configurable per-api-key and per-route. You can set priority/region and fallback policies (e.g., prefer us-east, fallback to us-west on SLO breach). We'll attach a sample routing policy JSON.

3) Request/response schema (chat vs completions): For agent-style Q&A we recommend chat with structured outputs (tool-calling) for determinism. Key notes: 
  - max_tokens governs generation length; recommend setting conservative user-side caps and using truncation/summary pre-processing for long contexts.
  - stop sequences are supported; for streaming+tool-calling we emit a tool-call event before streaming tool arguments, then resume streaming the tool output.
  - Streaming semantics: we support chunked token streaming and a final 'done' event. If you need guaranteed read-after-write ordering for tool calls, we can enable a no-interleave mode.

4) Embeddings & rerankers: For semantic search we suggest 1536 dims (depends on chosen model); batch size 64-128 for CPU-bound vectorization, higher on GPU. For rerankers we usually compute candidate scores via a dedicated rerank endpoint (cheaper and more deterministic) rather than heavy generation. We can provide a sample rerank scoring call.

5) Sample artifacts: attaching a short integration plan and a Drive link with SDK snippets.

Proposed next steps:
- I: Technical deep-dive with Aditya and Laura (30–45 min) to validate auth/routing and streaming semantics — are you available Fri 4/23 10am PT?
- II: POC kickoff (1 week) once we agree on model choices and routing.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding Northbridge's questions. They want a short POC: embeddings + reranker + chat agent with tool-calling. Key asks we need to answer before the Friday sync:

- Example routing policy we can drop into their infra (prefer us-east, fallback us-west; per-route).
- Concrete guidance on streaming + tool-calling: example sequence (client -> chat stream -> tool-call event -> tool output stream -> final response) and whether we have any SDK guarantees about interleaving.

Can one of you draft a concise reply/snippet and I'll send it to Oliver/Sejal. Also Aditya, if you can include an example tokenization note (how we report token usage and recommendations for max_tokens budgeting), that'd be great.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Northbridge discovery: SDK auth, routing & request/response schema questions

Quick draft answers and snippets below — feel free to paste into the external reply. I'll attach a small SDK snippet bundle for their infra team.

AUTH
- Recommended: Server-side short-lived tokens via our token-exchange endpoint. Flow: Customer uses their long-lived API key in a protected backend to call Redwood token-exchange API -> returns a short-lived token (exp 1h) scoped to route/model. Advantages: limited blast radius, easy rotation.
- OAuth2 client_credentials: supported for Private deployments where they want a delegated corporate identity. mTLS: available for air-gapped/on-prem installs.

ROUTING
- Policies are JSON objects you can apply per-api-key or per-route. Example (pseudocode):
  {"policy": [{"region":"us-east-1","priority":100},{"region":"us-west-2","priority":50,"fallback_on_slo":true}]}
- Policy resolution order: per-route > per-key > global. You can set a circuit-breaker SLO threshold to trigger fallback.

STREAMING + TOOL-CALLING (behavioral semantics)
- Sequence we recommend: 1) Client opens chat stream -> 2) Model emits partial tokens -> 3) Model emits "tool_call" event with tool name + args (structured JSON) -> 4) Client invokes tool (blocking or async) and streams tool output back into Redwood via the tool-output stream -> 5) Model resumes streaming final answer.
- Token accounting: tokens emitted as tool_call args are counted as output tokens; tool-output streamed back is treated as new input tokens if you feed them into a resumed generation. For POC keep max_tokens conservative (e.g., 256 for agent responses) and use truncation for context > model_limit.
- Stop sequences: honored immediately when encountered in generation. For streaming we send an explicit finalization event so clients can know when to stop listening.
- No-interleave mode: togglable flag to prevent interleaving of unrelated streams when multiple tool calls are active. Use if you need strict ordering guarantees.

REQUEST/RESPONSE EXAMPLE (pseudo-raw)
- Chat request (client->Redwood):
  POST /v1/chat/stream
  body: {"model":"rwd-chat-2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Find me docs about refund policy"}],"stream":true,"tools":["kb_search","rerank"]}

- Model stream (Redwood->client):
  {"event":"tokens","data":"Finding relevant docs..."}
  {"event":"tool_call","tool":"kb_search","args":{"q":"refund policy","top_k":10}}

- Client calls tool and streams results back to Redwood tool-output stream.

EMBEDDINGS / RERANK
- Embedding dims: 1536 is a good default for our medium models.
- Batch size: 64 for CPU; 256+ on GPU.
- Reranker: Use our rerank endpoint for deterministic scoring — cheaper than full generation when you only need ranking scores. If you need semantic rewrite of a result, do a light generation step as a second pass.

ATTACHMENTS
- I'm attaching a small SDK snippet package (sdk-snippets.zip) with examples for token-exchange, routing policy application, and a streaming tool-calling flow.

I'll hand this back to Mina to schedule the Friday slot.

-Aditya
Software Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
